newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to firm on strong bids, crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to firm on strong bids, crude gains.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were expected to edge higher, riding on crude strength and firmer bids from a major oil company, traders said.
Most traders said the current market is overpriced. "The market has gone up because of the recent tension between Iraq/US and should ease off," said one trader.
"Unless the market sheds by $10, the chinese are not going to be buying," said another trader.

Traders said recent strong buying interest from a major oil company has supported prices. The major told Reuters he is still keen to buy and there is a lack of offers. Traders said there are at least three sellers in the market-two majors and a local trader.
The local trader was heard to be bringing in South Korean supplies.
Traders said demand from China remained weak and Indian's tender demand remained uncovered.
Bunker 180-cst on Tuesday were indicated at $114-$115 per tonne.
Singapore September swaps were quoted firmer at $114/$115 per tonne, fairly stable from Tuesday's levels.
